author: Abigail Velez
title: Classes resume 1 day after student fell to his death at school in Highland Park - NewsBreak
text:
By Abigail Velez ,
8 hours ago
Students and staff returned to Franklin High School on Thursday as authorities continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of a student who fell from the fourth floor of a campus building.
A growing memorial lined the school’s entrance, giving students a place to remember the classmate who died on Wednesday.
PREVIOUS REPORT: Student dies after 4th-floor fall at high school in Highland Park, witnesses say
A student died at Benjamin Franklin High School in Highland Park, prompting a lockdown that lasted nearly three hours.“I thought it was terrible. Because someone died. It’s a bad thing. It’s a tragedy,” student Chance Pedroza said.
The fall happened shortly before 1 p.m., when students said they heard a loud thump. Police said the student dropped from the fourth floor and landed in the quad below.
“The bell was about to ring. I heard screams from inside the school. I didn't know what was going on,” student Ryan Moman said. “I kind of felt scared for the kid because I didn’t know what he was going through. For him to fall off from the fourth floor is kind of scary.”
Investigators are focusing on the moments before the fall. Witnesses said there was a fight between students.
“Everybody was running, and it was so bad and so sad,” a cafeteria worker, who wished to remain anonymous, said.
The school reopened on Thursday morning, but some students were not ready to return.
“I’m not going to go to school for the rest of the week. I think it’s too much,” Pedroza said.
The cafeteria worker, who remained shaken by what she experienced, questioned whether the campus should have reopened so soon.
“A lot of students, they saw it,” she said. “I think it’s better to close the school to give time to the students to calm down.”
Some students who returned to campus raised concerns about bullying. Parents also expressed fear about sending their children back to school.
“I’m just scared, like, I don’t even want to send them to school today or for the next couple of days,” one parent said. “I don’t know. I haven’t slept. I’ve been crying all night thinking about it, you know, because that could’ve been my boy up there.”
Police have not identified the student who died. His classmates remembered him as a positive and caring friend.
Students and community members plan to honor him at a vigil at 5 p.m. Thursday outside the school.
“I just have no words. Everybody is sad for this, and the least that I can do is come over and light up a candle and say a prayer for his family,” parent Rogelio said.
